newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Poland joins chorus of criticism of Belarus.
newsitem.headline: Poland joins chorus of criticism of Belarus.

text.p: Poland on Tuesday joined the growing chorus of criticism of Belarus President Alexander Lukashenko, saying that any country that wanted to be part of Europe had to respect democratic rules.
"Human rights and fundamental freedoms have to be observed in Belarus...since common values are the prerequisite of a united Europe," Polish President Aleksander Kwasniewski said.

Addressing the final day of an Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe (OSCE) summit in Lisbon, Kwasniewski told Lukashenko he must respect his own country's constitution and ensure free parliamentary elections.
"There is no other way of constructing a democratic parliament," he said. The blunt language followed a stream of criticism of Lukashenko from leader after leader on Monday.
Criticism of Lukashenko, said by foes to have dictatorial tendencies, has centred on last month's referendum which gave him wide powers and which critics say was neither fair nor free.

But the unusually harsh criticism of a participating OSCE member, which has come from the United States, Britain, Ireland and the European Union as well as neighbouring states like Ukraine and Lithuania, has left Lukashenko unmoved.
"It would be counterproductive to try to exert pressure on us or try to interfere in our internal affairs," Lukashenko said on Monday, calling the referendum completely democratic.
The only major ally Belarus has left is Russia, with which the economically struggling country of 10 million is seeking closer integration five years after the Soviet Union's collapse.

Aligning himself with Russia and adding to the frustration of other leaders, Lukashenko joined Russian Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin on Monday in condemning NATO's plans to take in other countries of eastern and central Europe.
Poland, Hungary and the Czech Republic, expected to be the first to join NATO, have all told the OSCE conference of their continued determination to join the security alliance.
"I am confident that the enlargement of NATO eastwards is not only in Poland's but indeed in the whole continent's vital interest," Kwasniewski said in his address to the summit.
Poland is due to take over the chairmanship of the OSCE in 1998, about the time NATO is expected to start accepting its first new entrants from the east.
